summary: Validated the Anexos permission matrix (AnexosModal.jsx) governed by quote_history. Admin level fully validated end-to-end via UI. Consulta (read) level NOT directly testable via /quotes UI because srubio@megasoft.com.ve has cotizaciones='none' and therefore cannot access the /quotes grid where the Anexos button lives — verified by API (GET /api/auth/login → cotizaciones: 'none', quote_history: 'read'). Code review of usePermission + AnexosModal confirms the gating logic is correct: a hypothetical user with cotizaciones>=read AND quote_history=read would see only downloads (no Subir, no papelera). Backend RBAC already validated by pytest (6/6 PASS) per main agent context.
action_items: OPTIONAL: To complete UI-level validation of the Consulta tier on the /quotes-driven AnexosModal, provide a test user with cotizaciones:read AND quote_history:read (e.g., grant srubio cotizaciones:read temporarily, or seed a new fixture user). Note: srubio CAN access /historical-quotes, but that page uses a different component (HistoricalAnexosModal.jsx), not the AnexosModal.jsx targeted by this matrix.
critical_code_review_comments: AnexosModal.jsx (lines 44-46): canUpload=canEdit, canDelete=isAdmin — correctly derived from usePermission('quote_history'). For role==='user' the hook returns canEdit only when permissions.quote_history==='edit' and isAdmin=false; therefore a quote_history='read' user would correctly see neither Subir (anexo-upload-btn-*) nor papelera (anexo-delete-*). Logic is sound.
usePermission.js (lines 20-26): admin short-circuit returns canEdit=true,isAdmin=true → AnexosModal shows Subir + papelera, matching Admin expectation (visually confirmed).

HistoricalQuotes.jsx imports HistoricalAnexosModal — a separate component from AnexosModal.jsx. The two modals are independent; this iteration's matrix applies only to AnexosModal.jsx opened from /quotes via quote-anexos-btn-*.
